Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Charlie Scharf commented, “Our third quarter results reflect broad-based growth, higher earnings, and stronger returns. Diluted earnings per share increased to $1.87 in the third quarter, up 13% from a year ago. Our ROTCE4 increased from 14.7% during the first nine months of 2025 to 16.2% during the same period this year and 16.3% in the third quarter. Both average loans and average deposits increased 11% from a year ago.”
“Wealth and Investment Management revenue grew 12% versus a year ago, Commercial Banking grew 6%, Consumer Banking and Lending grew 5%, and Corporate and Investment Banking revenue increased 3%. These increases were partially offset by lower revenue from our venture capital investments and lower lease income following the sale of our rail car leasing business in the first quarter,” Scharf added.
“Key growth metrics across our businesses showed continued strength. In the quarter we had continued growth in consumer primary checking accounts, opened more than 660,000 new credit card accounts, and auto originations increased 15% from a year ago. Wealth and Investment Management client assets grew 11%, investment banking and markets fees from Commercial Banking clients grew 25%, and within Corporate and Investment Banking, overall Banking revenue increased 8%, including M&A revenue increasing 30% and both equity capital markets and investment grade underwriting fees increasing 33%. While Markets revenue was relatively stable from a year ago, equities revenue grew 21%,” Scharf continued.
“Expenses declined from a year ago even though revenue-related expenses increased 15%. Expense savings have funded much of the investments that are making the company stronger, improving our capabilities, and positioning us for continued future growth,” Scharf continued.
“While economic uncertainty exists and consumer sentiment remains mixed, our data shows that our consumer and business customers are doing well. Consumers are spending more, loan delinquencies are low, and deposit and investment balances have grown. Businesses continue to have strong balance sheets and losses remain low. While higher interest rates, higher oil prices and persistent inflation create risks to the economy, strong positive forces such as the investment in AI infrastructure, high employment levels and consistent wage growth continue to outweigh the risks,” Scharf added.
“I’m proud of the Wells Fargo team and we will continue to remain vigilant about risk as we build for the long term,” Scharf concluded.

Third Quarter 2026 vs. Third Quarter 2025
◦Net interest income increased 5%, driven by higher loan and investment securities balances, the impact of lower interest rates and balance sheet growth in our Markets business, and fixed rate asset repricing, partially offset by the impact of lower interest rates on floating rate assets, higher deposit costs reflecting growth in interest-bearing commercial deposits, and a modest decline in noninterest-bearing deposits
◦Noninterest income decreased 1%, as higher investment advisory fees, deposit-related fees, investment banking fees, and card fees, were more than offset by lower trading gains, lower lease income related to the first quarter 2026 sale of our rail car leasing business, lower equity gains reflecting lower results from our venture capital investments, as well as lower mortgage banking income
◦Noninterest expense decreased 1%, driven by the impact of efficiency initiatives, including an 8% reduction in headcount, lower severance expense, and lower lease expense, partially offset by higher revenue-related compensation expense reflecting improved performance and an increase in technology and equipment expense. Third quarter 2025 included $296 million of severance expense
◦Provision for credit losses in third quarter 2026 included an increase in the allowance for credit losses, reflecting a higher allowance for commercial and industrial loans and auto loans driven by higher loan balances, partially offset by a lower allowance for commercial real estate loans
◦Income tax expense in third quarter 2026 included $170 million of discrete tax benefits related to the resolution of prior period matters

Operating Segment Performance

Consumer Banking and Lending offers diversified financial products and services for consumers and small businesses. These financial products and services include checking and savings accounts, credit and debit cards, as well as home, auto, personal, and small business lending. We also provide personalized wealth management and financial planning services through our branch channel.

About Wells Fargo
Wells Fargo & Company (NYSE: WFC) is a leading financial services company that has approximately $2.3 trillion in assets. We provide a diversified set of banking, investment and mortgage products and services, as well as consumer and commercial finance, through our four reportable operating segments: Consumer Banking and Lending, Commercial Banking, Corporate and Investment Banking, and Wealth & Investment Management. Wells Fargo ranked No. 38 on Fortune’s 2026 rankings of America’s largest corporations.
